status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-11-17, committed before any Criteo model was fitted or evaluated. Edit only by writing v5.
purpose: Hillstrom (64,000 customers) cannot show whether an uplift model beats random targeting: the power calculation needs about 284,000 customers. This protocol tests the SAME question on a randomized dataset about 200x larger and asks how the answer changes with training-set size, including a Hillstrom-sized training set.
relation_to_other_protocols: Independent of v2/v3 and of the exported case HILLSTROM_EMAIL_2008. Nothing here changes reports/campaign_case.latest.json. Criteo is a different (anonymised, advertising) setting; it is a methodological replication, not evidence about Hillstrom customers.

data.name: Criteo Uplift Prediction Dataset v2.1 (Diemert, Betlei, Renaudin, Amini; AdKDD 2018)
data.licence_note: Released by Criteo AI Lab for research (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per the dataset card). Raw file is gitignored and never redistributed here.
data.design: randomized advertising exposure: roughly 85% treated, 15% control; outcome = conversion (about 0.3%). Randomization is by Criteo, so treated-minus-control differences are causal estimates.

split.rule: one seeded random permutation of all rows (seed 20261117): first 20% of the permutation = TEST (touched once, after all fits), remaining 80% = TRAIN POOL. Training subsets are drawn from the pool only.
split.test_use: The test split is read once, for the evaluation specified below. No tuning, no peeking at test results to change settings.

candidates.S_LOGIT: baseline: single logistic regression on features, treatment and treatment x feature interactions, L2 C=1.0 on standardised features
candidates.T_LOGIT: two separate logistic regressions (treated, control); score = difference of predicted probabilities
candidates.S_HGB: single HistGradientBoosting classifier with the treatment flag as a feature (max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.1, max_iter 200, min_samples_leaf 200, l2 10)
candidates.T_HGB: two HistGradientBoosting classifiers (same settings); score = difference

training_sizes.note: Draws are independent random subsets of the TRAIN POOL (seeds derived from 20261117). Hyper-parameters are fixed above for every size; nothing is tuned per size.

estimands.policy: contact the top 25% of the TEST split by model score
estimands.primary_metric: additional conversions per 1,000 contacts among the selected 25% (treated conversion rate minus control conversion rate, times 1,000)
estimands.random_reference: the same estimator on the whole TEST split (equals random targeting in expectation)
estimands.primary_contrast: GAP = selected-25% uplift per 1,000 minus whole-test uplift per 1,000
secondary: paired difference in GAP versus S_LOGIT at the same training subset
estimands.uncertainty: customer bootstrap on the test split, 100 resamples (Poisson(1) weights), the same weights for all candidates of one fit so differences are paired; 95% percentile intervals

decision_rules.model_beats_random_at_a_size: the 95% interval of the GAP excludes zero (lower bound > 0) in a majority of that size's draws
decision_rules.challenger_beats_baseline_at_a_size: the 95% interval of the paired GAP difference versus S_LOGIT excludes zero (lower bound > 0) in a majority of that size's draws
decision_rules.reading: If no candidate beats random at the Hillstrom-sized training set but one does at larger sizes, the Hillstrom 'not stable' verdict is a data-size limit, not evidence that targeting cannot work. If none beats random at any size, say so. Report whichever outcome occurs.

honesty: Nothing in this protocol was fitted or looked at before commit; only column names and row count were inspected.
Accuracy is not reported: conversion is about 0.3%, so 'nobody converts' scores about 99.7%.
Results describe advertising exposure in an anonymised dataset; no profit claim is made.
Four candidates x 11 subsets are all reported; there is no selection of the best run.
